newsitem.title: UK: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.
newsitem.headline: Bond market wrapup - late European trade.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets looked at 1630 GMT on Monday.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were nearly a point lower at noon, battered after a jump in the Chicagoland business barometer capped off a string of surprisingly robust regional purchasing managers reports, analysts said.
GERMANY - Bund futures ended lower, pulled down by weaker Treasuries. Ranges now seen before FOMC meeting. Tietmeyer and Waigel speaking in Frankfurt on Tuesday.
Futures: September Bunds on LIFFE at 101.5, down 0.33
BRITAIN - UK gilts fell by over half a point in low volume trade as budget uncertainty plagued the market and rate rise fears set in, traders said.
The September gilt contract ended 17/32 lower at 113-30/32. Futures: September Long gilts on LIFFE at 113.96, down 0.5

FRANCE - Bond futures drifted lower in a lacklustre session marked by a negative reaction to stronger-than-expected U.S. economic releases the day before the Federal Reserve's policy setting council meets. Traders said the contract began to head south after failing to break through resistance at 129.52/54 after several tests early in the day, trailing the Bund market lower, but remained above key technical support at 129.06. Futures: September Long bond on MATIF at 129.18, down 0.04

ITALY - The debt market ended mixed with cash bonds holding on to slim gains but Btp futures slipped into negative territory in the wake of other markets after U.S. treasuries fell on a strong June Chicago Purchasing Managers' index.
Futures: September Long bond on LIFFE at 133.97, down 0.11

JAPAN - The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower due to hedge selling by dealers, traders said. "There was talk that a city bank had sold 10-year JGBs, and that dealers who bought the bonds from them sold JGB futures for hedging purposes," a brokerage house trader said.
Futures: September JGB future on LIFFE compared with Tokyo close at 124.16.

EUROBONDS - Peripheral currencies dominated Eurobond activity, in what is expected to be a quiet week. The World Bank launched a 1.0 trillion lire 10-year bond, setting a liquid benchmark for the sector. The European Investment Bank added a further 250 billion lire to its February 2007 step-down bond. Retail offerings were launched in dollars and marks. Issuance would be dampened by the FOMC meeting, July 4th U.S. holiday, the British budget and holidays in Hong Kong.
